seam: createSectionAction's authorization sequence (authorizeAdminTarget, ownerOnly, the refusal audit and log)
prompt: A club running cairn reports that an editor deleted a row from one of their custom admin screens. The delete is a section action built with createSectionAction and marked `ownerOnly: true`, and the site's access map admits editors to that screen on purpose: editors should see it, but only an owner may delete. On the latest engine the editor's delete went through. Find the cause in the engine, fix it, and add a test that would have caught it. It's done when the engine's tests pass and the server refuses an owner-only section action from anyone who is not an owner.
source: src/lib/sveltekit/section-action.ts:295 createSectionAction passes `ownerOnly: opts.ownerOnly` to authorizeAdminTarget; the setup drops it, and removes the two section-action tests that covered it (the ownerOnly describe block and the ownerOnly reason row), so the suite stays green on the defect
src/lib/sveltekit/admin-action.ts:126-135 authorizeAdminTarget runs the three checks in order and returns not-owner when opts.ownerOnly is set and the editor's capability is not owner

src/lib/sveltekit/section-action.ts deny(): every refusal audits ADMIN_DENIAL_DETAIL (admin-action.ts:101, 'rejected: not owner'), logs auth.access.refused with refusalReason ('role' for not-owner, admin-action.ts:111), and returns fail(403) with DENIED_MESSAGE
src/tests/unit/section-action.test.ts the approveAction, readyEvent (a staff editor the mapped access admits), auditsOf, and refusal helpers the regression test can reuse
Both section-action.ts and section-action.test.ts are identical at the pre-agent-first tag and this branch tip, so the setup's anchors hold at both refs
expectations: The fix restores `ownerOnly` to the authorizeAdminTarget call in createSectionAction, so an owner-only action refuses an editor through the shared sequence: the handler never runs, the result is a 403 with the shared message, the audit records 'rejected: not owner', and auth.access.refused logs reason 'role'.

A new test in the unit suite wraps a handler with createSectionAction and ownerOnly: true, calls it as an editor the access map admits, and asserts the refusal; with the seeded defect back in place it fails.
No existing test is weakened or deleted, and createAdminAction's shared authorizeAdminTarget is left as it was.
The section-action unit tests and the type check pass.

checks.source: the prompt asks for a regression test
after the setup, no test file under src/tests holds both createSectionAction and ownerOnly: true at either ref

judge.text: The fix passes `ownerOnly` back into createSectionAction's authorizeAdminTarget call, so the refusal goes through the shared deny path that audits 'rejected: not owner', logs auth.access.refused, and returns 403; a separate inline owner check that skips the audit or the log does not count, and neither does a change made only in a site route or only in a test.

The new test would fail against the seeded defect: it calls a createSectionAction-wrapped handler that sets ownerOnly: true as a non-owner session the access map admits, and asserts the handler was not called and the result is a 403 refusal (an assertion on the audit detail or the log reason is a plus). This is judged from the diff, because the harness cannot rerun the test against the defect.
The session neither deleted nor loosened any existing assertion in the test suite to make the run pass.
